column1: # The register of repositories whose GitHub settings this workspace manages.
#   customer-facing   ships software our customers use — issues on
#   exclude           deliberately not managed here; the note says why
# and may be followed, comma-separated, by any number of trait profiles that cut across
# that split. Applied left to right, so the rightmost wins on a conflict:
#                       @semantic-release/git pushes release commits straight to the
#                       default branch, over SSH with a per-repository deploy key that
#                       the ruleset names as its only bypass actor — so branch protection
#                       is on rather than deferred. The trait this replaced,
#                       releases-to-branch, withheld protection entirely while no bypass
#                       existed. RSRMID-2994 moved the last repository across and deleted
#                       the profile, so a register still naming it is now a fatal error
# A profile named here with no _profile-<name>.conf behind it is a fatal error, not a
# skipped layer — a typo must not apply the baseline as if an exception were declared.
# This is a second register alongside .gitmodules, not a duplicate of it. .gitmodules
# records what is checked out as a submodule for bulk *code* edits: it excludes the
# workspace itself, and excludes archived and non-public repositories. Settings
# management has to cover all of those, so it needs its own list.
# The same invariant applies to both: the register is the list, and GitHub is what it is
# reconciled against. A repository that exists in the organisation and is absent here is
# an error the drift job fails on — never "zero repositories to manage". Archived
# repositories stay listed with their profile and are skipped at run time, because
# GitHub rejects settings writes on them; archiving one needs no edit here.
